26	 * raw object (image+alt, combined colour/size, quantity, stepQuantity) — ready for whichever
27	 * future step decides how a real page hands data down, without having modified any of those
28	 * existing files.
29	 *
30	 * `CartLineItem` models the REAL runtime shape a basket line item has by the time it reaches
31	 * those leaves: the un-overridden base cart page never passes the raw `basket.productItems[i]`
32	 * alone — it merges it with the matching full `Product` (fetched separately via `useProducts`)
33	 * before handing it down: `product={{...productItem, ...productsByItemId[productItem.itemId],
34	 * price: productItem.price, quantity: ...}}` (see
35	 * `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-item-list/index.jsx`, the
36	 * `<ProductItem product={...}>` call). `imageGroups`/`variationAttributes`/`variationValues`/
37	 * `stepQuantity`/`name` all come from that merged-in `Product` half, not from
38	 * `ShopperBasketsTypes.ProductItem` itself (confirmed against its generated fields — it has no
39	 * image/variation/stepQuantity fields at all beyond its own `{[key: string]: any}` catch-all).
40	 *
41	 * Both halves are `Pick`'d, not intersected raw (zm-tester, SFCC-11 step 3.4 finding): the real
42	 * generated `ProductItem` type carries the identical `{[key: string]: any}` catch-all the comment
43	 * above already calls out on `Product`. Intersecting it raw would silently resolve a typo'd field
44	 * name (or a nonexistent one) to `any` instead of a compile error — empirically confirmed harmless
45	 * today (every real access below is spelled correctly) but a real, latent gap a future edit could
46	 * hit silently. `Pick`ing both halves closes it the same way on both sides.
47	 */
48	type CartLineItem = Pick<ShopperBasketsTypes.ProductItem, 'itemId' | 'productId' | 'quantity' | 'productName'> &
49	  Pick<
50	    ShopperProductsTypes.Product,
51	    'imageGroups' | 'variationAttributes' | 'variationValues' | 'stepQuantity' | 'name'
52	  >;
53	
54	type CartItemImage = {
55	  src?: string;
56	  /**
57	   * Always a string, never undefined — even when there's no image at all (falls back to the
58	   * item's own name, then `''`). See `selectCartItemImage`'s own doc comment for the fallback
59	   * chain and why this differs from `productListCardMapper.ts`'s `toCardImage`, which returns
60	   * `undefined` for the whole image on a miss instead.
61	   */
62	  alt: string;
63	};
64	
65	type CartItemMapperResult = {
66	  itemId?: string;
67	  productId?: string;
68	  name: string;
69	  image: CartItemImage;
70	  combinedAttributes: string;
71	  quantity?: number;
72	  stepQuantity: number;
73	};
74	
75	/**
76	 * Matches `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-derived-product.js:38`'s own
77	 * `product?.stepQuantity || 1` exactly — reused as a value, not a shared import, since that hook
78	 * itself isn't a pure function this module can call (it's stateful, `useState`-backed).
79	 */
80	const DEFAULT_STEP_QUANTITY = 1;
81	
82	/**
83	 * Selects this line item's display image, always returning a defined `alt` even when there is no
84	 * image at all (unlike `productListCardMapper.ts`'s `toCardImage`, which returns `undefined` for
85	 * the whole image on a miss — a PLP card can legitimately skip rendering entirely when it has
86	 * nothing to show; a cart line item cannot, per this step's own pass criteria).
87	 *
88	 * The lookup itself reuses `findImageGroupBy` exactly as
89	 * `overrides/app/components/item-variant/item-image.tsx:70-73` already does (same `viewType:
90	 * 'small'` / `selectedVariationAttributes` call) rather than reimplementing image-group matching.
91	 */
92	const selectCartItemImage = (item: CartLineItem): CartItemImage => {
93	  const image = findImageGroupBy(item.imageGroups, {
94	    viewType: 'small',
95	    selectedVariationAttributes: item.variationValues,
96	  })?.images?.[0];
97	
98	  return {
99	    src: image?.disBaseLink || image?.link,
100	    alt: image?.alt || item.productName || item.name || '',
101	  };
102	};
103	
104	/**
105	 * Combines the colour and size variation values into the single string the Figma cart-item spec
106	 * calls for, reusing the exact mechanism
107	 * `overrides/app/components/item-variant/item-attributes.tsx:98,148-150` already uses for its own
108	 * `combineAttributeValues` behaviour (`getDisplayVariationValues(...)` then
109	 * `Object.values(...).join(', ')`) rather than reimplementing string-combining from scratch.
110	 *
111	 * Ordering is inherited from that same call, not independently re-sorted here: it reflects
112	 * whichever order the incoming `variationValues` object's own keys are in (see
113	 * `getDisplayVariationValues`'s `Object.entries(values).reduce(...)`,
114	 * `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/product-utils.js:30`). This is the
115	 * identical mechanism `item-attributes.tsx`'s own docblock (line 31) already cites as producing
116	 * "Lilac Sand, One size" (colour, size) for real Zimmermann catalog data —
117	 * `product-item/index.tsx`'s docblock (line 44) corroborates the same combined-string behaviour
118	 * generically ("colour, size") without repeating that specific example. This function inherits
119	 * that already-verified behaviour rather than re-guaranteeing the order independently.
120	 */
121	const selectCombinedAttributes = (item: CartLineItem): string => {
122	  const variationValues = getDisplayVariationValues(item.variationAttributes, item.variationValues);
123	  return variationValues ? Object.values(variationValues).join(', ') : '';
124	};
125	
126	/**
127	 * Maps one basket line item (already merged with its full product data — see this file's own
128	 * module docblock) to a plain display-data shape: image, name, one combined colour/size string,
129	 * and quantity/stepQuantity passed through. Pure function, no hooks — keeps every consumer in B3
130	 * prop-driven with no data-fetching hook in a leaf, per this step's own plan text.
131	 */
132	export const selectCartItemProps = (item: CartLineItem): CartItemMapperResult => ({
133	  itemId: item.itemId,
134	  productId: item.productId,
135	  name: item.productName || item.name || '',
136	  image: selectCartItemImage(item),
137	  combinedAttributes: selectCombinedAttributes(item),
138	  quantity: item.quantity,
139	  stepQuantity: item.stepQuantity || DEFAULT_STEP_QUANTITY,
140	});

> **BUILD HANDOFF: start at `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-11/HANDOFF.md`.**

> Figma spec; `plan.md` is the executable plan; `findings.md` is the gate.


**Written:** 2026-09-16
**Branch at time of writing:** `feature/SFCC-831-689_country-language-mismatch` (NOT the build branch — a
fresh `feature/*` off `develop` is needed before any cart work starts)
**Scope:** card-by-card requirements pass over 7 Cart stories, ahead of a bundled build.
**Status:** all 7 cards read, all ACs pulled and adjudicated. No code written. No Jira updated.

The ACs do **not** live in the Jira description — they are in custom field `customfield_10231`
("Acceptance Criteria", project-scoped, textarea). Fetching only the description misses them
entirely. Some return plain text, some return ADF (`{type: "doc"}`) — SFCC-315/270/795 came back
as ADF and needed flattening.

---

## 1. The bundle

All 7 are Epic SFCC-11 (Cart), SFCC Sprint 5 (active, 2026-09-07 → 2026-09-21), label `Squad-A`,
assigned to Marcel, status **Ready for Development**.

| SFCC-275 | Cart Page – Button Group | High | CAI-010 |

### Bundle-shape decision

One gather pass and one plan across all 7 (done — this document). **Not** one mega-PR.
Rationale: a single PR converts 7 independently-mergeable units into one all-or-nothing unit;
one change-requested story would block the other six. Cart also spans two squads' Tier 2

in both code-owner reviews at once, and AGENTS.md Hard Rule #10 requires explicit scope
confirmation before touching more than one protection tier in one change.

build as one PR. Accepted deliberately.

VERDICT: IN SCOPE — 4 files, all named in plan.md's own manifest (§3 lines 113-114, restated in step 3.4 text lines 318-329), all 4 pass criteria met with evidence I reproduced myself, zero Tier 1/2 files touched, working tree contains nothing beyond the 4 files at every point I checked it.

## 1. Diff scope trace
`git status --porcelain=v2 --untracked-files=all` — run before, during, and after my own verification work — returned the identical 4 lines every time: `overrides/app/pages/cart/cartItemMapper.ts`, `.../cartItemMapper.test.ts`, `overrides/app/utils/maxOrderQuantity.ts`, `.../maxOrderQuantity.test.ts`. Nothing else, ever. plan.md:113-114's file-manifest table names exactly these two file+test pairs with `create` as the action. plan.md:846 maps commit 10 → step 3.4 → message `feat(cart): SFCC-250 cartItemMapper and maxOrderQuantity util` — exact match to what you stated. Every layered fix you described (docblock self-correction, 2 mutation-driven tests, the `CartLineItem` `Pick` narrowing) lives inside these same 4 files — none of it introduced a 5th file.

## 2. Tier check
`overrides/app/pages/cart/` = Tier 3, CODEOWNERS:153 (`@ZimmermannAU/pwa-squad-a`) — and CODEOWNERS' own header comment above that block states Tier 3 is "plain squad ownership, not a protection gate," i.e. a normal single-reviewer PR, no code-owner approval required. `.claude/rules/squadA.md:37` does list this path as Squad A territory, and `.claude/session-notes.md:24` confirms the whole SFCC-11 epic carries the `Squad-A` label and is assigned to you — so even taking the draft squad doc literally, this step never leaves the requesting owner's own lane. `overrides/app/utils/` has no CODEOWNERS entry at all; plan.md:114 calls it "untiered | none" outright, matching reality. Neither file is near Tier 1 (frozenFiles.md) or Tier 2 (protectedFiles.md).

## 3. Type-safety fix — reproduced independently, not re-read
Backed up `cartItemMapper.ts` byte-for-byte, appended a throwaway line to the real file (`item.variationAttribute`, a deliberate typo of `variationAttributes`), ran the project's real `npx tsc --noEmit`. Result: `overrides/app/pages/cart/cartItemMapper.ts(142,67): error TS2551: Property 'variationAttribute' does not exist on type 'CartLineItem'. Did you mean 'variationAttributes'?` — exact match to the claim. Restored the file from the backup immediately after; `diff` confirmed byte-identical restoration, and a final `git status` confirmed the working tree still shows only the original 4 files. The `Pick<...> & Pick<...>` narrowing at `cartItemMapper.ts:48-52` is real.

## 4. item-attributes.tsx — confirmed correctly left alone
Diffed `overrides/app/components/item-variant/item-attributes.tsx` against `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/item-variant/item-attributes.jsx` directly: `useCurrentBasket`, `usePromotions`, `useProducts`, `useProduct` are in the **base file too**, same call sites — carried over verbatim by the copy-first port. `git log --all -- .../item-attributes.tsx` shows exactly two touches, `22ca34c9` (copy-first port) and `9991c918` (restyle), both SFCC-270, both well before this step. I ran pass criterion 3's grep exactly as plan.md:327 specifies it and got the same non-empty result you did. It's genuinely not this step's to fix: `item-attributes.tsx` isn't named anywhere in step 3.4's manifest or pass criteria, neither new file imports or touches it, and going in to silence that grep now would be exactly the "fixing a bug in a component means touching the hook/utility it calls" pattern Hard Rule #5 forbids.

## 5. Everything else checked
- `npx vitest run` on both new test files myself: 2 files, 11 tests, all green (6 = 5 documented cases + the Infinity mutation-catch; 5 = 4 documented cases + the stepQuantity-fallback mutation-catch). Both added tests tighten verification of behaviour the plan's own criteria already named ("not a broken cap," "stepQuantity passed through") — no new branch, no new file, not scope creep.
- Pass criterion 4: `product-detail/index.tsx` absent from git status (untouched); no `MAX_PURCHASE_QUANTITY` anywhere in the new files — `maxOrderQuantity.ts` uses its own `DEFAULT_MAX_ORDER_QUANTITY`, exactly as plan.md:322 instructs.
- `npx eslint` on all 4 files directly: zero output, zero violations.
- Full-project `npx tsc --noEmit` post-restore, grepped for either filename: no hits.
- `.claude/registry/*.md` shows zero churn (not in git status) — nothing to flag either way; these are pure-logic modules, not components/hooks the registry tracks, so no churn was ever expected.
- The HANDOFF.md correction you described lives outside this repo (`~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-11/HANDOFF.md`), so it doesn't factor into the verdict, but I checked it anyway: the strikethrough + correction is genuinely at lines 56-65, and its cited authority rule ("§3/§4 are unchanged and authoritative") is real, at line 19 — not a fabricated citation.

## Unverified gaps (mine)
- Didn't check every individual cited line number inside the new docblocks char-for-char (`item-attributes.tsx:98,148-150`, `product-item/index.tsx:44`, `use-derived-product.js:38`) — verified the claim each citation supports, not each exact line pointer.
- Didn't re-derive the Tester's full 5-item mutation sweep from scratch — reproduced the one claim that most needed independent proof (the compiler error) and ran the resulting tests, rather than re-running an unchanged wave of checks.
- Didn't run the full project test suite or full lint — scoped to the 4 files this step touches, since nothing else changed.

## What Marcel is missing
Pass criterion 3, as literally worded in plan.md:327, can never actually return empty — not because of anything in this step, but because `item-attributes.tsx`'s base-ported hooks are permanent. If a future gate or reviewer takes "grep returns nothing" as the literal bar instead of "the two new files introduce no hook," it reads as failing forever, on every future cart commit, for a reason unrelated to that commit's correctness. Worth narrowing the criterion's wording (or scoping the grep to just the new files) before it trips up a less-informed check down the line.
